title: Raktanchal Is Back for Its Final Season. The Gang Wars Move to the State Assembly This Time.
excerpt: The gritty Hindi crime drama that turned Amazon MX Player into appointment viewing returns July 16 — and this time, the battle between Vijay Singh and Waseem Khan has an election to fight.
body:
If you have spent the last four years wondering what happened after **Vijay Singh** and **Waseem Khan** tore each other apart across the badlands of Purvanchal, the answer arrives on Wednesday. **Raktanchal Season 3** drops on **Amazon MX Player** on July 16, and the show is done pretending that violence and politics are separate industries.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=D1J2zKsOL2o</youtube>

The third and final season of one of India's grittiest web series shifts its battlefield from the dusty hinterlands of eastern Uttar Pradesh to the corridors of Lucknow power — where mafia muscle meets electoral machinery, and the line between a gangster and a politician disappears entirely.

## The Setup

Directed by **Ritam Srivastav** and written by **Siddharth Mishra**, the new season picks up in early-2000s Lucknow, where state assembly elections are about to turn every old grudge into a fresh body. **Vijay Singh** (played again by **Kranti Prakash Jha**) is trying something new — running for public office, attempting to dismantle the mafia system from the inside. It is the kind of pivot that sounds noble on paper and suicidal in practice, especially when your arch-nemesis has other ideas.

**Waseem Khan**, played with coiled menace by **Nikitin Dheer**, is not about to let Vijay clean up a system that keeps him fed. He forms new political alliances — the kind sealed with threats, not handshakes — to eliminate Vijay once and for all. What follows, if the teaser is anything to go by, is a season-long collision of betrayals, backstabbing, and open warfare for ultimate control of Uttar Pradesh.

> The teaser serves as a chilling reminder that some rivalries never truly fade.

## The Cast

Beyond the central rivalry, the ensemble has expanded to match the ambition. **Karan Patel**, **Mahie Gill**, **Rajesh Kumar**, and **Vikram Kochhar** all take on pivotal roles. Two new power players — **Saraswati Devi** and **Virendra Pratap Singh** — enter the brewing struggle, adding layers of complexity to a political landscape already drenched in blood. Nine episodes. No filler. Pure Purvanchal.

## Where to Watch — And It's Free

Here is the detail that matters most for diaspora viewers: **Raktanchal Season 3 is free**. It streams exclusively on Amazon MX Player, which is available across mobile devices, connected TVs, the Amazon shopping app, Prime Video, Fire TV, JioTV, and Airtel Xstream. No subscription required. No paywall. No excuses.

For NRI audiences who have been following the show since its debut in 2020, this is the resolution they have waited for. The first two seasons built a loyal fanbase with their unflinching portrayal of power, caste, and criminal enterprise in India's heartland — a world that feels authentically raw in a streaming landscape increasingly dominated by glossy urban thrillers.

## Why It Matters

Raktanchal was never Mirzapur. It never had the budget, the star power, or the marketing muscle. What it had was conviction — a willingness to tell a specific story about a specific place without smoothing out the edges for a metro audience. The show's depiction of Purvanchal's political-criminal nexus drew comparisons to the real-life histories of the region's strongmen, and its refusal to glamorize violence gave it a weight that slicker productions sometimes lacked.

The third season promises to raise those stakes further. With elections as the backdrop, the series is no longer just about who controls the streets — it is about who controls the machinery that runs the state. That is a story India knows well, and one that Raktanchal is uniquely positioned to tell.

All nine episodes of **Raktanchal Season 3** arrive on **Amazon MX Player** on **July 16, 2026**.
